subject: Granular evidence request: EU + APAC hosting & PrivateLink controls
messages:
From: Santiago Ruiz <s.ruiz@medivita.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@medivita.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Residency + PrivateLink evidence needed for procurement slack

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement at Medivita has a tight deadline: we need a compact evidence set to satisfy our security panel for an upcoming pilot. Can you provide the following by next Wednesday (2025-12-10)?

- SOC 2 report summary (high level is fine) and statement of any carve-outs.
- SIG responses or CAIQ answers for controls that relate to: network egress, VPC isolation, keystore/ HSM partitioning, operator access. We don’t need every control — just the ones the security reviewers have flagged (I can attach the list).
- PrivateLink / VPC deployment diagram showing where traffic exits (if any), and confirmation whether any customer traffic will traverse non-EU/APAC egress points when hosted in those regions.
- A short statement (1 paragraph) confirming Redwood’s ability to do a private deployment in our EU tenant and an APAC tenant (if required) and what the operator separation boundaries look like.

Attachments: medivita-security-ask-2025.pdf (we’ll send after this thread).

Appreciate a point person we can loop in on any clarifying Qs.

—Santiago
Senior Security Program Manager
Medivita Health
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Santiago Ruiz <s.ruiz@medivita.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Dec 2025 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency + PrivateLink evidence needed for procurement slack

Santiago — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Irene (security) and Marissa (account lead).

High level plan:
- Irene will assemble a compact SIG/CAIQ slice focused on the controls you called out and attach a SOC 2 one-pager.
- We'll include a PrivateLink architecture diagram showing regional egress and an operator boundary sketch.
- We can provide a short signed statement confirming EU and APAC private deployments and operator separation.

Timeline: aim to deliver an initial bundle by Wed, 2025-12-03 EOD for your internal review; final by 2025-12-08. If that works, we’ll proceed and ask one quick clarifying Q below.

Quick Q: for the CAIQ/SIG slice — do your reviewers want specific control IDs called out (e.g., NIST/CCM mapping), or is a control-level yes/no + short note sufficient?

Irene/Marissa — can you confirm availability to pull the artifacts?

Thanks,
Neha
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, Santiago Ruiz <s.ruiz@medivita.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 02 Dec 2025 08:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency + PrivateLink evidence needed for procurement slack

Hi all — I’ll own the artifacts. Deliverables we’ll attach in the initial bundle (Wed EOD):

1) redwood-soc2-summary-2025.pdf — 2-page summary that includes scope (services in scope), date of most recent audit, and any carve-outs.

2) sig-control-responses-compact.xlsx — a focused spreadsheet with the following tabs: 
   - Network/Egress (SIG IDs + short narrative)
   - Keystore/HSM (control notes, rotation cadence, KMS region partitioning)
   - Operator Access & Separation (how operator access is scoped for Private deployments)

3) privatelink-architecture-diagram.png — regional diagrams for EU and APAC showing: PrivateLink endpoints, peering, and where (if any) traffic egresses to other regions.

Notes / clarifications (short):
- Egress: hosted instances pinned to an EU region do not traverse US egress points for data plane by default. We’ll call out the exception cases (managed control plane telemetry and panic-fallback routes) and how those are handled.
- Keystore: for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS with an operator-keystore separation model; we’ll provide the operator access checklist.
- Redactions: we will sanitize low-level keys/operational logs; audit artifacts will be redacted to remove customer-specific identifiers.

Attachments included in initial email: redwood-soc2-summary-2025.pdf, privatelink-architecture-diagram.png, sig-control-responses-compact.xlsx

If Medivita can send the short list of flagged SIG/CAIQ control IDs, I’ll prioritize those rows. Otherwise we’ll include the default subset targeted above.

—Irene
Head of Applied Security | Redwood Inference
From: Santiago Ruiz <s.ruiz@medivita.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@medivita.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 02 Dec 2025 12:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency + PrivateLink evidence needed for procurement slack

Thanks, Irene — that sounds perfect. A couple quick follow-ups: 

- Can you add a short line in the SOC 2 one-pager that describes data flow for inference requests (tokenization & model execution) and whether any inference logs are stored outside the region?
- We’ll attach the flagged control IDs in a follow-up (should be < 15 items).
- Legal would like a draft DPA clause referencing region-bound hosting and customer-managed keys — can you share a draft we can start with? If easier, attach a Word doc.

Also, can you confirm whether Redwood offers per-region SLA targets for latency for Private deployments (we only need a directional statement for the panel)?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Santiago
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Santiago Ruiz <s.ruiz@medivita.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 03 Dec 2025 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency + PrivateLink evidence needed for procurement slack

Santiago — sending a short delivery plan and links. We’ll push the initial zip to the Drive link below by EOD: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/medivita-evidence/pack-2025

What you’ll get in the initial bundle (pack-2025):
- redwood-soc2-summary-2025.pdf (includes a two-paragraph inference-dataflow note and confirmation that inference-level logs are retained only in-region unless customer elects cross-region export)
- privatelink-architecture-diagram.png (EU and APAC diagrams with egress callouts)
- sig-control-responses-compact.xlsx (we left empty rows for the 15 flagged IDs you’ll send)
- dpa-draft-medivita.docx (template clause for data residency & customer-managed KMS — we’ll tailor language with Legal if needed)

Short answers to outstanding asks: 
- Per-region SLA: For Private deployments we provide configurable latency targets via Dedicated capacity reservations; for an initial panel statement we will confirm expected p95 latency ranges (region dependent) and attach a sample performance profile once we confirm the target model and sequence length. We’ll include a directional sentence in the pack.
- Operator separation: Irene’s spreadsheet includes explicit controls and an operator onboarding checklist; for Private deployments we support customer-owned operator roles and MFA-enforced operator access via Bastion jumphosts.

Next steps: Medivita sends flagged SIG IDs and we’ll populate the sheet and return a final bundle by 2025-12-08. If you want a 30-min sync to walk through the artifacts, we can do Thu morning.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Lead | Redwood Inference
